entities.description: Card 1 of the Lenormand. A horseman arriving swiftly. Traditionally linked to news coming quickly, a young man, or a message on its way. Associated with the Nine of Hearts and the ace of hearts in some traditions.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: News, messages, a young man, swift arrival, visit, communication incoming

entities.description: Card 2 of the Lenormand. A four-leaf clover. Represents small but genuine luck, brief good fortune, and fleeting opportunities that must be seized quickly.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Small luck, brief opportunity, good fortune, chance, optimism, carefree

entities.description: Card 3 of the Lenormand. A sailing ship on the sea. Represents travel, especially by water or long distance, commerce, foreign matters, and the journey toward a distant goal.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Travel, journey, foreign lands, commerce, adventure, long-distance movement

entities.description: Card 4 of the Lenormand. A traditional house or home. Represents family matters, domestic life, security, property, and the stable foundation of one's personal life.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Home, family, security, property, stability, domestic life, household

entities.description: Card 5 of the Lenormand. A great tree, often an oak. Represents health, vitality, deep roots, slow growth, spirituality, and the life force. Matters of long duration.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Health, vitality, slow growth, deep roots, spirituality, life force, long duration

entities.description: Card 6 of the Lenormand. Dark and light clouds. Represents confusion, uncertainty, hidden truths, and unclear situations. The dark side of the clouds indicates problems; the light side, clearing.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Confusion, uncertainty, hidden matters, lack of clarity, doubt, temporary obstacles

entities.description: Card 7 of the Lenormand. A coiled serpent. Represents a rival, an untrustworthy woman, deceit, temptation, complexity, and indirect paths. Can also represent wisdom and transformation.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Deceit, rival, indirect path, complexity, a cunning woman, temptation, wisdom

entities.description: Card 8 of the Lenormand. A funeral coffin. Represents endings, completion, serious illness, grief, but also transformation and putting something to rest. Not necessarily literal death.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Endings, completion, illness, grief, transformation, something over, serious change

entities.description: Card 9 of the Lenormand. A bunch of flowers. Represents gifts, invitations, social pleasures, beauty, appreciation, and good feelings. A generally positive card of grace and social harmony.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Gift, invitation, pleasure, beauty, appreciation, happiness, social grace

entities.description: Card 10 of the Lenormand. A harvesting scythe. Represents sudden cuts, accidents, harvest, decisive action, and the abrupt end of something. Can indicate danger from sharp implements.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Sudden end, harvest, decisive cut, accident, danger, abrupt change, severance

entities.description: Card 11 of the Lenormand. A whip or bundle of rods (also called The Rods or The Broom). Represents conflict, repetitive actions, aggression, arguments, sports, and discipline.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Conflict, argument, repetition, aggression, discipline, sport, discussion

entities.description: Card 12 of the Lenormand. Two birds, often owls or other birds. Represents communication, chatter, negotiations, anxiety, and the exchange of information — sometimes excessive talk.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Communication, gossip, chatter, negotiation, two of anything, anxiety, small worries

entities.description: Card 13 of the Lenormand. A young child. Represents new beginnings, innocence, small matters, naivety, and actual children. Something new, small, or in its beginning stages.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: New beginning, innocence, small matter, child, naivety, something fresh and new

entities.description: Card 14 of the Lenormand. A fox. Represents cunning, self-interest, caution, deception, and the need to be wary of those who may not have your best interests at heart. Also work and career.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Cunning, self-interest, deception, caution, work, a cunning person, shrewd action

entities.description: Card 15 of the Lenormand. A powerful bear. Represents strength, power, authority, financial matters (particularly investments and savings), and a powerful older person, often maternal.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Strength, power, authority, finances, a powerful figure, boss, maternal energy

entities.description: Card 16 of the Lenormand. Stars in the night sky. Represents hope, clarity, higher guidance, wishes, and spiritual matters. A very positive card indicating success and divine favor.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Hope, wish, clarity, guidance, success, spiritual matters, inspiration

entities.description: Card 17 of the Lenormand. A stork. Represents change, transformation, movement, and new arrivals — classically a pregnancy or birth, but more broadly any positive transformation.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Change, transformation, positive change, pregnancy, return, migration, new arrival

entities.description: Card 18 of the Lenormand. A dog. Represents loyalty, friendship, trusted companions, and support. A faithful friend or advisor. Generally very positive.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Loyalty, friendship, trusted companion, support, faithful advisor, good friend

entities.description: Card 19 of the Lenormand. A tall tower or government building. Represents authority, government, legal matters, isolation, large institutions, and solitude. Unlike the tarot Tower, this is not inherently negative.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Authority, government, institution, solitude, legal matters, structure, isolation

entities.description: Card 20 of the Lenormand. A public garden or park. Represents society, public life, gatherings, social events, networks, and the public sphere. Meetings and social occasions.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Society, social gathering, public life, network, meeting, community, social media

entities.description: Card 21 of the Lenormand. A great mountain. Represents obstacles, challenges, delays, and blockages. Something stands in the way. Effort and time are required to overcome.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Obstacle, challenge, blockage, delay, enemy, difficulty, slow progress

entities.description: Card 22 of the Lenormand. A fork in the road. Represents choices, decisions, alternatives, freedom to choose, and crossroads moments. Multiple paths are available.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Decision, choice, alternative paths, freedom, crossroads, options available

entities.description: Card 23 of the Lenormand. Mice gnawing. Represents loss, theft, deterioration, worry, stress, and things being eaten away gradually. Something is being depleted or stolen.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Loss, theft, deterioration, worry, stress, depletion, something eaten away

entities.description: Card 24 of the Lenormand. A red heart. Represents love, romance, kindness, emotional matters, and matters of the heart. A classic card of love and affection.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Love, romance, kindness, affection, emotional happiness, generosity, passion

entities.description: Card 25 of the Lenormand. A ring. Represents commitment, contracts, marriage, agreements, partnerships, and cycles that repeat. A binding promise or legal obligation.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Commitment, contract, marriage, agreement, cycle, partnership, binding promise

entities.description: Card 26 of the Lenormand. A closed or open book. Represents secrets, knowledge, education, research, and hidden information. What is known and unknown.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Secrets, knowledge, education, research, hidden information, learning, mystery

entities.description: Card 27 of the Lenormand. A written letter or document. Represents written communications, documents, messages, paperwork, and correspondence. News in written form.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Written communication, document, message, paperwork, letter, email, contract

entities.description: Card 28 of the Lenormand. A male figure. Represents the male querent or a significant man in the reading. Used as a significator for male-identified persons.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: A man, the male querent, masculine energy, a significant male figure

entities.description: Card 29 of the Lenormand. A female figure. Represents the female querent or a significant woman in the reading. Used as a significator for female-identified persons.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: A woman, the female querent, feminine energy, a significant female figure

entities.description: Card 30 of the Lenormand. A white lily. Represents purity, virtue, calm, wisdom of age, sexuality in some traditions, and a peaceful, serene quality. Often associated with older, mature persons.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Purity, virtue, peace, maturity, wisdom, harmony, chastity or sensuality

entities.description: Card 31 of the Lenormand. A radiant sun. Represents success, vitality, happiness, positive outcomes, and great good fortune. One of the most positive cards in the deck.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Success, happiness, vitality, achievement, great fortune, clarity, warmth

entities.description: Card 32 of the Lenormand. A crescent moon with a face. Represents recognition, fame, intuition, psychic ability, the subconscious, romance, and emotional depth. Can indicate honors received.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Recognition, fame, intuition, psychic sensitivity, romance, honors, subconscious

entities.description: Card 33 of the Lenormand. A key. Represents solutions, answers, unlocking, certainty, destiny, and access. This card often indicates that a matter will be resolved positively.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Solution, answer, unlock, certainty, destiny, access, important revelation

entities.description: Card 34 of the Lenormand. Fish, often shown with a barrel or water. Represents financial abundance, business, flow of money, depth, and independence. Primarily a card of material plenty.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Financial abundance, business, flow of money, depth, independence, prosperity

entities.description: Card 35 of the Lenormand. A ship's anchor. Represents stability, security, long-term persistence, endurance, work, and the steady holding of one's position. Groundedness and security.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Stability, security, endurance, persistence, work, groundedness, long-term success

entities.description: Card 36 of the Lenormand. A Christian cross. Represents burden, suffering, fate, spiritual matters, moral weight, and karmic lessons. Something that must be borne with acceptance.

extendedData.uprightMeaning: Burden, suffering, fate, karma, spiritual test, moral weight, destiny to be accepted
